newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia UES bond issue to start Oct - minister.
newsitem.headline: Russia UES bond issue to start Oct - minister.

text.p: A convertible bond programme by Russian national power company Unified Energy System (UES) will begin about in October when investor activity is at its peak, Interfax news agency quoted Deputy Prime Minister in charge of privatisation Alfred Kokh as saying on Wednesday.

The stake, which the company and officials have said will be on 1.5-5.0 percent of shares, would raise at least five trillion roubles and proceeds would be used to pay public sector wage arrears, he told a news conference.

UES has already announced it will issue convertible bonds with at least a three-year conversion maturity on up to five percent of its shares. The government will use the proceeds to pay trillions of roubles (billions of dollars) in back wages.
The government, which owns 52.7 percent of UES, and the company itself may both put up shares to back the bonds and could share the proceeds.

The government is considering preserving only a 50 percent plus one share majority stake in UES, using the rest for the bond programme. UES officials have said a further 2.3 percent of authorised shares which have not yet been issued could be covered by the bonds.

The government has already approved a general programme for the bonds, which will follow the launch of an American Depositary Receipt Programme to improve share liquidity through foreign trade. Details of the size of the bond issue will be presented in a detailed government plan expected soon.
